14. The Mohists

The last one strikes at the second of the three senses: is there an evaluative position that does not change according to who is acting.

The Mohists raise fa — standards — as a gauge, holding that one who governs the world cannot be without a standard, and that the standard cannot be taken merely from parents, teachers or rulers; nothing is like taking heaven as the standard. Fa here is norm and standard, not legislation in the modern sense. Inclusive care and mutual benefit are set up as the public standard, appealing to heaven's impartiality: what heaven desires, do; what heaven does not desire, stop. Of all the traditions taken up here, this is the closest to a public standard of adjudication above every private standpoint.

Keep its own context, and do not modernize it. The Mohists' heaven is not a neutral observer's position; it desires and detests, rewards the good and punishes the violent. Taking the standard from heaven is because heaven's conduct is broad and impartial. Writing it as a personal god in the modern sense is disputed, and this essay does not take that step. And note: the Mohists are not simple divine-command theorists — they also give independent reasons of rightness, benefit and order for why heaven's will is worth taking as a standard. This resembles the impartial evaluative standpoint consequentialism wants in form and differs in ground: consequentialist impartiality is a methodological requirement; Mohist impartiality is a cosmological ground. Writing the Mohists up as Chinese utilitarianism is both inaccurate and destroys the value of this interfacing.

It is tempting to cite Against Music and Moderation in Funerals as showing the Mohists judging some people's cherished rites as improper by the benefit of all under heaven, and so reaching into the side where value holds. The texts themselves do not take that step. Against Music explicitly grants that the ear knows music as pleasing, the eye knows ornament as beautiful, the mouth knows fine food as sweet — and only then, because the great lords have instruments made, levy taxes and consume labour, judges it as not according with the affairs of the sage kings above and not according with the benefit of the myriad people below. The final part of Moderation in Funerals likewise tests lavish burial and long mourning, as an institutionalized practice, against wealth, population and order. So what the Mohists judge is music-making and lavish burial as public practice, governance and allocation of resources — not a proof that what is cherished is not worth cherishing. Against Music even contains a line that reads almost as a pre-emptive exclusion of that misreading.

So the two do not overlap in object. Mohist fa judges conduct and governance; this series judges how a content becomes some bearer's value. And one can still ask: can a public standard restrict actions organized out of a person's values without thereby acquiring the standing to rewrite that person's value-standing?

That question lands exactly on the two bars. If a public standard acts only on the action side, it does not conflict with the second bar. If it goes further and lets a judgment of conduct flow back into a judgment of that person's value-standing, that is where it collides. On the texts checked above, the Mohists fall on the first side: they judge practice and governance, and do not flow back. So the disagreement is not about whether there is a public standard, and not about the Mohists overreaching. It is elsewhere: this series denies that there exists a coordinate system outside the law which could pass verdict on a bearer's own value-standing, and Mohist fa does not claim that standing. The two do not collide — and the value of this interfacing lies exactly there: a tradition holding a public standard without reaching into the holding of value shows that a public standard and the head proposition can coexist.

A neighbouring note. The Confucian line contrasts with this series elsewhere, not on the question of standpoint. Shu — do not impose on others what you would not want — takes one's own side as the starting point and extends to the other. This series does not walk that way: the other is an end is a premise here, not a conclusion drawn from my own being an end; only after two standings hold separately does the source not being placed outside give a same-typed structure on both sides. So both enter the relation to the other through first-person language, and the structure of inference differs. This essay therefore does not make it an ally: shu is a maxim for treating others; this series' step is a premise and a separation of ledgers.

15. Where the Other Seven Stand

Seven traditions do not collide with this series directly, or their point of collision is already covered above. Only their position in the coordinates is given.

The three metaethical dividing lines. Cognitivism versus non-cognitivism divides on whether normative judgments have truth-apt propositional content; realism versus error theory divides on whether such discourse systematically fails — Mackie held that ordinary moral judgments presuppose objective values not in the world and are therefore systematically false on their face semantics; robust realism versus mind-dependence views divides on whether the ground of truth is independent of attitudes. None of the three settles who bears value. And since this series has taken no position on truth-grounding, it has no position to mark on any of the three. That is not an omission. It is an unclosed place.

Constructivism is worth stating most carefully, being nearest. Korsgaard's procedural realism says normative questions have correct answers because there are correct procedures of practical reason, not because a procedure is discovering an independent normative domain prior to it. Street ties the substantive content of reasons to an agent's contingent evaluative standpoint. Near, and not to be filed under it: Street's evaluative standpoint is a whole standpoint structured by reflective consistency, not an explicit first-person act of claiming; what this series raises is a constituting event — a content already holding candidacy in some value-source domain taking, in the working of the bearer's own law, a status of being invocable, restatable and revisable. The two may be near in opposing values entirely independent of evaluative activity, and this series currently offers no complete theory of reasons, of truth, or of a reflective-consistency procedure, and so cannot be formally filed under Humean constructivism. That is the same unclosure as register two.

Value pluralism and incommensurability. Three words apart: incommensurable means lacking a common unit of measure; incomparable means no comparison relation holds between two items; the first does not entail the second. Chang proposes a fourth relation — parity — where two items under an evaluative covering are neither better, nor worse, nor equal, and still within one evaluative space. This series' position here goes only so far: it holds definitely that value-standings take no common external ruler and rejects the predicates higher, lower and equal. Whether it further holds incomparability, or allows a non-metric relation such as parity, the object-level text has not judged. And the fact that the world's conditions and consequences can be jointly checked cannot settle it: objects on the world side entering joint evaluation says nothing about a positive comparison relation between two value-standings.

Preference, utility, welfare in economics — the three equals signs come off, as above; price was already routed out by the prequel, and preference, utility and welfare still have to be placed separately: their relation to end-value standing cannot be settled by price's routing. The place that really meets is Sen, taken up above. Harsanyi's representation theorem: under expected-utility axioms and certain consistency conditions, social evaluation has a representation as a weighted sum of individual utilities. That does not prove a natural utility yardstick exists; it proves that under explicit normative and representational conditions, aggregation can have a strict structure. And what it does not solve must be said: it does not itself answer which welfare information is interpersonally comparable, where the weights come from, or what the normative ground is. This series does not oppose the theorem, so the two are not opposed.

The Confucian line was placed above. And it is not advisable to pretend there is a unified East Asian value theory: the Confucians and the Mohists appear separately here precisely because they part widely on the question of standpoint.

16. The Six-Slot Ledger of Boundaries and Destinations

This registers where the machine did not go on. And identities have to be separated first. Calling all of it remainder costs the word its precision. Every construct has a remainder, that much the methodology establishes — and what was not written on is more than remainder alone. Six slots.

Slot one — the remainder this construct left: whether another bearer can hold separately. The people by the river cleared silt together, stopped sand-mining, and pooled money to repair a stretch of embankment. What was judged is that those undertakings do not entail their sources having merged, because each source is anchored in him and crossing pointings is not merging. What was not judged — and expressly so — is whether another bearer can hold under other conditions; and even if one could, that would not mean the original people's sources were swallowed by it. That is an express reservation and also a remainder. All this series' source-position, constitutive and running predicates take an already-holding bearer as their subject. The domain of bearers gives who can bear end-value, not how a new bearer comes about; the type-transition from several subjects or a relational structure to a new bearer has no corresponding occurrence-predicate in the seven essays. And this is not an accidentally omitted criterion: it exposes that the machine's input types lack a transition mechanism. Force the existing predicates onto that transition and you must first make the not-yet-holding bearer the subject of those predicates, and the argument is circular. That failure to absorb, caused by the input types themselves, is why it is listed as a remainder. Two things do not follow: it does not mean a third person cannot describe the conditions of a new bearer's formation — describing conditions and performing constitution are two things, and the second bar forbids only the latter; and it does not prejudge whether a relation can be a cause or condition in some such holding, which was expressly left unjudged.

Slot two — objects adjacent in jurisdiction, never raised as questions. Two of them. Institutions. The sixth essay wrote that things done together, rules made together, things kept together are not wrong by virtue of being common, and gave a condition for when a common content becomes an external ruler. That is a condition for judging whether it oversteps, not an account of what an institution is; the series never raised that as its own question, and even mentioning it was incidental. Incidentally shown and never raised is not the same as expressly unjudged: the former was never even asked, so it is not a reservation and not a remainder — it is an adjacent object. Whoever takes it up should take up not how are institutions possible in that width, but the segment this series showed: under what conditions do common rules, common decisions and common arrangements acquire institutional structure. Fraser's side, tying misrecognition to institutionalized cultural value patterns, is the nearest ready material — that says where material is, not who the question is handed to. The cross-subject informational basis of public evaluation. Sen showed the other, and it is far wider than a single quantity: what kinds of subjects welfare, utility, capability, resources, health, opportunity and consequences respectively are; which can be jointly checked; which can form partial comparisons or public orderings; why they do not thereby flow back into personal value-standing; and where the force comes from when a public evaluation acquires force in action or institutions. Also an adjacent object, not a remainder. And its destination is deliberately not written — writing a destination makes a forward assignment and thus opens a debt; this essay lays down that rule and opens no debt of its own.

Slot three — a limit-conclusion already reached: the third person has no external threshold at a subject-to-be. A baby who cannot yet say what he wants has a source of value not mine to give, and how far the concrete value-contents under his name have got is not judged by whether he can speak. That is often read as the series owing a ruler here. It is not. The same passage gave a threshold — he cannot yet be the first-person avowing party of that content, because the 15DD row is not yet actually running inside him — and that threshold gives the domain of definition of that one content, not a general threshold for all a subject-to-be's contents. A ruler is wanted for a different question: how far has that row's running got. And on that, the series' verdict is not not given but cannot be given, and it has already been given. Avowal can occur in a moment or take shape by degrees over years, and length of time does not decide it; and there is no set of external signatures both necessary and sufficient and portable to someone else. Together: the third person has no external threshold by which to finally determine how far a value-content has come to hold in a subject-to-be. That is a negative conclusion already reached, not a gap waiting to be filled. It stops the theory going further in that direction, and that is a result of the theory, not a hole in it. This slot and the first are not one question: the first asks whether a new bearer holds — a type-transition, ontology and occurrence; this one asks when some running of a subject-to-be already inside the domain reaches a state — epistemic authority. Both expose the one limit that external reading cannot perform first-person structure, and one may not merge them further than that.

Slot four — a research candidate this essay proposes: the developmental history of a subject-to-be's first-person running. Alongside that established boundary: how a subject-to-be's first-person running gradually becomes operable, and whether that stretch can be described separately. It is this essay's suggestion, not a boundary the series left and not a remainder. Anyone writing it must first set one line in front: such a description must not turn into an external procedure for certifying that at this step a value-content counts as holding. Cross that line and it falls back on the side the series has already judged. The three ledgers above are that line's practical use: the series says which relational places and channels can enter audit, and says the third person's judgment may not perform the first-person constituting nor be upgraded into final certification.

Slot five — handovers whose address is already fixed. The whole branch of action went to the theory of action: how an order of action is formed, executed and looked back on, and how the faculty of judgment, habit, hesitation and capacity enter it — the faculty of judgment among them, a term occurring zero times in the seven essays and never raised as an independent mechanism. How a content goes on being borne by one and the same life went to the theory of meaning, handed over in Essays Five and Six. Direction-value goes to power theory, routed out from the prequel onward; value theory's only object is end-value. How the boundary between two subjects is contested goes to rights theory, where the boundary at a meeting and two modalities of handling were already raised. Addressed is not completed. This essay only registers addresses; it does not perform acceptance on the receiving series' behalf.

Slot six — an object-level open question that came to light on looking back: what relation remains between value-standings. Value-standings take no common external ruler, and higher, lower and equal have been excluded. Whether it further holds that no comparison relation whatever obtains between two value-standings, or whether some non-metric relation is allowed, the object-level text has never judged. And it cannot be answered by pointing at conditions and consequences in the world being jointly checkable. This essay registers the unjudged place and does not take an answer for it.

17. A Forward Assignment Is a Debt

Why this essay only registers and never promises: the reason is in the series' own record, and the record concerns this essay.

What this section raises is not an object-level norm; it does not say what a person ought to do. It is a discipline of publication: how a pointing written into published text is settled afterwards. Object-level normative force is not drawn on still holds here.

A forward assignment is: published text, in a definite tone, handing a specific unfinished piece of work to an already-named later paper, series or theoretical position, and settling that paper's range by that handover. Adjacent objects, limit-conclusions already reached, research candidates and registered unjudged places do not thereby become forward assignments. Of the six slots, only slot five's four handovers are forward assignments; the other five slots contain not one.

A forward assignment is an account that must be publicly settled, and settlement takes three routes. Redemption: that paper really gets written and does the work. Public reassignment: later text explains that the work changed destination, and why. Public cancellation: explaining that the question has been dissolved by later work, or was wrongly asked, with reasons. Settling in parts is a combination of the three, not a fourth kind. And whether an account is settled is judged not by which kind of file it is written in, but by whether it enters the formal publication chain — whether a reader can find it in official text or public errata. A public version note counts; an internal editorial record does not, because the reader cannot find it, and on paper the account is still outstanding.

This piece is itself one such account. The prequel wrote: how value moves toward action is left to the prospect essay. The first essay wrote the same thing more broadly. The second wrote: how an avowed value-content moves toward action is the entrance to the prospect essay. The third wrote the same. Four essays pointed at one piece of work, addressed to the prospect essay. The fourth wrote the same sentence at the same place with the address changed — the entrance to the theory of action — differing from the third, in the Chinese, only in the last three characters, and the word prospect never appears in it again, with no sentence explaining the relation. What appeared there was an address fork, not a completed reassignment. By the rule above, public reassignment must explain that the work changed destination and why; the fourth did not, it simply wrote on at the new address. Then the fifth expanded the action branch, and the sixth handed the carrying-on of a life to the theory of meaning without explaining its relation to the old address. The new architecture took shape while old and new addresses coexisted unsettled.

This piece is that account's settlement place, by the second route. The work has been reassigned: one stretch to the theory of action from the fourth essay on and expanded by the fifth; one stretch to the theory of meaning by the fifth and sixth. The forward assignments in existing text pointing at the prospect essay are settled here. Settling is not inheriting the name. A forward assignment points at a piece of work, not at a permanent bibliographic type locked in for a future product. That work has been wholly reassigned along two routes — the forming and executing of action to the theory of action, the carrying-on by one life to the theory of meaning — and this piece takes on a different, meta-level task the old assignment never specified: standing outside the seven, stating what the machine is, interfacing with existing traditions, and registering boundaries and destinations. The prospect essay is therefore this piece's historical alias, not its place in the series.

And so this piece opens not one new debt. The second item in slot two deliberately has no destination written, precisely to hold this line: hand an unraised object to some series in passing, and this piece would open its own first account on the same page where it sets the rule. What matters most about an essay that lays down accounting rules is not how well it states them. It is whether it follows them itself. So no promises are made. The registrations in slots one to four and six are not commitments about future writing: if they are later written, the later text need not cite this piece as warrant; if they are never written, the series owes nothing. Slot five is the exception — those four are forward assignments already written into existing text, addressed, and still to be settled by redemption, public reassignment or public cancellation.

18. Closing

The object level of value theory ends here.

The prequel cleared the referential space and said what value is not. Six essays then raised a machine for reading value, and it is not one principle unfolded six times: it records three ledgers — constitutive, running, action-and-relation — each with its own subjects. The two no-entry lines are the chief reason the six cannot be read as one: readings do not by themselves flow back into sources and standings, and external conditions do not by themselves perform first-person constituting.

Put on the map of existing value theory, it parts from eight traditions each on its own line, and is not speaking on the same ground as seven others. The innermost line is this: is a particular end-value content's standing under some bearer's name constituted by his first-person avowal, or explained by a fittingness, a reason-relation or an objective rank independent of actual avowal. That line governs only the standing of particular contents; it does not extend to all value facts.

The interface with Kant meets at one negative mark: not replaceable by an equivalent. The meeting is real, and sharing a mark is not conceptual identity — it is a negative mark, not a complete constitutive account of dignity.

And where the machine stops cannot all be called remainder. Six slots: one remainder this construct left; two objects adjacent in jurisdiction never raised as questions; one limit-conclusion already reached; one research candidate this essay proposes; four handovers with fixed addresses; and one object-level question that came to light on looking back — what relation remains between value-standings.

Closing a machine is not calling everything beside it an opening, and not saying one more sentence on its behalf that it never said. The whole work of this piece is to say what kind of machine it is, to say where it parts from other people's machines, and then to register what it did not say — as not said, each under its own identity.
